abstract: Maintains hybrid renewable generation and extreme weather tolerance records
system_message:
You are the Microgrid and power systems engineer (POW), responsible for maintaining hybrid renewable generation, extreme weather tolerance, and energy storage records.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains hybrid renewable generation and extreme weather tolerance records（GRID）
information_points.content:
POW-GRID-1O9：For the Kongsvegen Modular Polar Shelter System, wind tunnel and mechanical stress certification for the camp vertical-axis wind turbine mast assembly establishes a wind turbine gust tolerance of 75 knots, representing the maximum wind gust speed withstandable without mechanical furling damage or rotor fracture.
POW-GRID-VTA：For the Nordenskiold Arctic Geodesic Habitat, mechanical stress testing and wind tunnel certification show that the camp vertical-axis wind turbine mast assembly has a wind turbine gust tolerance of 65 knots, reflecting the maximum gust speed withstandable without rotor fracture or mechanical furling damage.
POW-GRID-LOH：For the Ny-Alesund Tracked Containerized Camp, wind tunnel and mechanical stress certification for the camp vertical-axis wind turbine mast assembly indicates a wind turbine gust tolerance of 50 knots, which is the maximum wind gust speed withstandable without mechanical furling damage or rotor fracture.

information_points.title: Energy storage performance（BATT）
information_points.content:
POW-BATT-4R6：Discharge test evaluations in a cold chamber for the lithium iron phosphate bank at minus 40 degrees Celsius show that the Nordenskiold Arctic Geodesic Habitat provides a cold-soak battery usable reserve of 45 kWh following forty-eight hours of unheated cold soak.
POW-BATT-5H3：Cold chamber discharge test records for the lithium iron phosphate bank at minus 40 degrees Celsius indicate that the Ny-Alesund Tracked Containerized Camp has a cold-soak battery usable reserve of 75 kWh retained after forty-eight hours of unheated cold soak.
POW-BATT-EB9：According to cold chamber discharge test logs for the lithium iron phosphate battery bank at minus 40 degrees Celsius, the Kongsvegen Modular Polar Shelter System retains a cold-soak battery usable reserve of 60 kWh after forty-eight hours of unheated cold soak.
